scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A continuum temperature singularity for a radial pair potential” (preprints/A-continuum-temperature-singularity-for-a-radial-pair-potential-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 228 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3c00f7387c84c30), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist an admissible radial difference-only pair potential Φ(x) = ϕ(|x|) on R3, a nonempty open interval I ⊂ (0, ∞), and one βc ∈ (1/2, 3/2) with the following properties. The potential satisfies ϕ(r) = o(r−3) as r → ∞. The free-cube limit (1.3) exists and is finite for every β > 0 and every density ρ > 0. For every ρ ∈ I, the finite one-sided derivatives at the same critical point satisfy D− β fΦ(βc, ρ) > D+ β fΦ(βc, ρ). Thus one potential and one critical inverse temperature give a strict canonical temperature singularity throughout I.
